text:
## Observations

1. Only floor cells can host humidifiers or count toward the answer. Desks do not block humidification because coverage depends solely on Manhattan distance.
2. The two humidifiers are interchangeable, so each unordered pair of distinct floor cells needs to be checked only once.
3. For a fixed pair, a floor cell contributes one to the total if its distance to either humidifier is at most \(D\), even if both humidifiers cover it.
4. There are at most 100 floor cells, so scanning every floor cell for every pair requires at most 495,000 floor-cell checks.
5. There are at least two floor cells, so a valid pair always exists. When \(D=0\), every pair covers exactly its two placement cells. When \(D=H+W-2\), every pair covers all floor cells.

## Solution sketch

> Only floor cells can host humidifiers or count toward the answer. Desks do not block humidification because coverage depends solely on Manhattan distance.

1. Read the grid and store the row and column of each `.` cell in a list. Let \(F\) be the length of this list. Use the list for both candidate placements and coverage checks.

> The two humidifiers are interchangeable, so each unordered pair of distinct floor cells needs to be checked only once.

2. Enumerate every pair of list indices \(a<b\). The strict inequality ensures that the placements are distinct and that every possible placement is considered exactly once.

> For a fixed pair, a floor cell contributes one to the total if its distance to either humidifier is at most \(D\), even if both humidifiers cover it.

3. For each pair, scan the floor list. Compute Manhattan distances using the absolute row difference plus the absolute column difference. Increment the pair’s count once whenever at least one distance is at most \(D\). Track the largest count and print it after all pairs have been checked.

> There are at least two floor cells, so a valid pair always exists. When \(D=0\), every pair covers exactly its two placement cells. When \(D=H+W-2\), every pair covers all floor cells.

4. Use the same procedure at both distance extremes. The inclusive distance check counts the placement cells at \(D=0\), and at \(D=H+W-2\) the distance between any two grid cells is within range. If there are exactly two floor cells, the procedure checks their single pair and returns 2.

> There are at most 100 floor cells, so scanning every floor cell for every pair requires at most 495,000 floor-cell checks.

5. Scanning the grid takes \(O(HW)\) time, and checking \(\binom F2\) pairs with \(F\) floor cells per pair takes \(O(F^3)\) time. The floor list uses \(O(F)\) extra space when the grid is read one row at a time.
